## Goals

-   Recognize non-independence in a dataset
-   Fit random-intercept models with `lmer()`
-   Use `marginaleffects` to report population-level effects

## Setup



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(marginaleffects)
```
:::



## The paired t-test, again



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
sleep2 <- sleep |> rename(drug = group)
t.test(extra ~ drug, data = sleep2, paired = TRUE)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Paired t-test

data:  extra by drug
t = -4.0621, df = 9, p-value = 0.002833
alternative hypothesis: true mean difference is not equal to 0
95 percent confidence interval:
 -2.4598858 -0.7001142
sample estimates:
mean difference 
          -1.58 
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_pair <- lmer(extra ~ drug + (1 | ID), data = sleep2)
summary(m_pair)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method [
lmerModLmerTest]
Formula: extra ~ drug + (1 | ID)
   Data: sleep2

REML criterion at convergence: 70

Scaled residuals: 
     Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
-1.63372 -0.34157  0.03346  0.31511  1.83859 

Random effects:
 Groups   Name        Variance Std.Dev.

 Residual             0.7564   0.8697  
Number of obs: 20, groups:  ID, 10

Fixed effects:
            Estimate Std. Error      df t value Pr(>|t|)   
(Intercept)   0.7500     0.6004 11.0814   1.249  0.23735   
drug2         1.5800     0.3890  9.0000   4.062  0.00283 **
---

Correlation of Fixed Effects:

drug2 -0.324
```


:::
:::



Same t value (−4.06), same p. Notice the model also estimates how much patients differ at baseline:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
VarCorr(m_pair)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
 Groups   Name        Std.Dev.
 ID       (Intercept) 1.68770 
 Residual             0.86974 
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_comparisons(m_pair, variables = "drug")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

```


:::
:::

## Repeated measures over time

`ChickWeight`: weights of chicks over 21 days on different diets. Each chick is measured repeatedly. We'll compare diets 1 and 2.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
cw <- ChickWeight |>
  filter(Diet %in% c("1", "2")) |>
  mutate(Chick = factor(Chick, ordered = FALSE), Diet = droplevels(Diet))
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(cw, aes(Time, weight, group = Chick, color = Diet)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.6) +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Individual chick growth trajectories](week12-tutorial_files/figure-html/fig-chicks-1.png){#fig-chicks width=672}
:::
:::



Ignoring the chick structure treats ~500 measurements as independent. Instead:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_cw <- lmer(weight ~ Time * Diet + (1 | Chick), data = cw)
summary(m_cw)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method [
lmerModLmerTest]
Formula: weight ~ Time * Diet + (1 | Chick)
   Data: cw

REML criterion at convergence: 3241.6

Scaled residuals: 
    Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
-3.2043 -0.5627 -0.1079  0.5666  3.4866 

Random effects:
 Groups   Name        Variance Std.Dev.
 Chick    (Intercept) 637.3    25.25   
 Residual             681.9    26.11   
Number of obs: 340, groups:  Chick, 30

Fixed effects:
            Estimate Std. Error       df t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)  31.5210     6.5269  41.5758   4.829 1.89e-05 ***
Time          6.7098     0.2661 313.1818  25.215  < 2e-16 ***
Diet2        -2.8874    11.2590  40.9863  -0.256    0.799    
Time:Diet2    1.8993     0.4411 310.2833   4.306 2.24e-05 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Correlation of Fixed Effects:
           (Intr) Time   Diet2 
Time       -0.411              
Diet2      -0.580  0.238       
Time:Diet2  0.248 -0.603 -0.416
```


:::
:::



Slopes within each diet (grams per day):



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_slopes(m_cw, variables = "Time", by = "Diet")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

 Term    Contrast Diet Estimate Std. Error    z Pr(>|z|)     S 2.5 % 97.5 %
 Time mean(dY/dX)    1     6.71      0.266 25.2   <0.001 463.6  6.19   7.23
 Time mean(dY/dX)    2     8.61      0.352 24.5   <0.001 437.4  7.92   9.30

Columns: term, contrast, Diet, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high, predicted_lo, predicted_hi, predicted 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_slopes(m_cw, variables = "Time", by = "Diet", hypothesis = "pairwise")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

  Term Estimate Std. Error     z Pr(>|z|)    S 2.5 % 97.5 %
 1 - 2     -1.9      0.441 -4.31   <0.001 15.9 -2.76  -1.04

Columns: term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::



Population-level predictions for a "typical" chick:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
predictions(m_cw, newdata = datagrid(Time = c(0, 21), Diet = c("1", "2")), re.form = NA)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

Columns: rowid, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high, weight, Chick, Time, Diet 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_predictions(m_cw, condition = c("Time", "Diet"), re.form = NA) +
  theme_minimal()
```
